schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The “Post-Doctoral Fellowship (PDF)” is a component of the “Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT”, implemented by the Digital India Corporation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India. The objective of the scheme is to promote R&D, create an innovative ecosystem, and enhance India’s competitiveness in the knowledge-intensive sectors of Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) and IT/IT Enabled Services (IT/ITES). This fellowship is meant for those who have a proven track record as evident from their research publications and recognitions. Support is provisioned for 225 Post-Doctoral Fellowships for candidates for a period of one year, to encourage specialized research in emerging areas.
schemeContent.benefits_md: ***Nature of Support:*** - **Research Fellowship:** ₹1.08 Lakh/Month - **Contingency Grant:** ₹1 Lakh for 1 year (on re-imbursement and pro-rata basis depending on the period spent under the award). The claim would be submitted by the awardee through respective institution to PhD Cell in prescribed format. - The fellowship is tenable only in India and can be implemented in any of the recognized & eligible academic and R&D institutions. - Contingency Grant can be used for minor equipment, consumables and similar items relevant to the research work. The host institution should provide necessary administrative and infrastructural support for the PDF fellow. - There is no provision for providing research personnel support under the scheme. The fellow is expected to undertake the research objectives by himself/herself during the entire duration of the fellowship. - PDF is a full-time assignment. The fellows are not eligible to receive any other fellowship from any Government or Non-Government source during the tenure of the fellowship. - Post-doctoral positions are non-transferrable. The research work is to be carried out in the same eligible institution at which PDF seat is allocated and the fellow is enrolled. ***Duration of Support:*** - The fellowship is purely a temporary assignment, and is tenable for a period of 1 year.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme wherein eligible institutions submit proposals requesting PDF seats against an active call for proposal by Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme, DIC, MeitY. <br> 1. The call for proposal for PDF seats will be notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ and/or email. 2. Proposals for allotment of PDF seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable number of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines. 3. The institution may design/have its own application form for advertisement of PDF; however, the guidelines for PDF are to be followed which must include the following: <br> 1. The PDF applicant should be an Indian citizen. 1. The PDF applicant must have obtained PhD degree from a recognized University with first class (in terms of grades, etc.) in all preceding levels and a good academic record throughout. 1. The eligible participating institution must ensure that the PDF applicant should have completed PhD within the past 5 years on the last date of submission of application to the institution. 1. The upper age limit for the fellowship is 40 years on the date of submission of application to the eligible participating institution. 1. A suitable Mentor/Guide under whom the proposed research would be carried out, must be identified by the institution. 1. Mentor/Guide of PDF fellow must hold a regular academic/research position in a recognized institution in India. He/she should hold a Ph.D. degree in Science or Engineering. 1. Preference would be given to the PDF applicants who have active industry linkages and their research proposal is directed towards industry specific problems. 1. The research proposal of the PDF applicant, to be submitted to the institution, should define clear objectives, outcomes and deliverables against the award. 1. PDF applicants currently in regular employment will not be considered. However, scientists or researchers with temporary positions in academia or research institutions would be considered however, they would be required to relinquish their current roles if selected for the fellowship. 1. PDF applicants should not have completed their PhD at the same institution where the PDF fellowship is to be awarded. 1. The applicant must have a proven track record as evident from their research publications and recognitions. 1. The applicant should not be availing any other fellowship. ***Discontinuation of the Fellowship*** 1. If any fellow wishes to discontinue the fellowship, the institution should inform PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY immediately. One month’s notice is to be given by the institution before the date of discontinuation. 1. The implementing institution should not incur any expenditure from the date of termination of the award/project or the date of resignation of the fellow. The institution will responsible for submission of work report and other requisite documents. 1. In case the post-doctoral fellow undertakes any full/part-time assignment, his/her PDF award under the scheme would be discontinued. 1. PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY reserves the right to hold/ stop/ discontinue the fellowship at any stage, if - Appropriate progress is not being made. - The grant is not being utilized properly. - Violation/ Non-compliance of guidelines. - Any other reason, which is deemed appropriate by PhD Cell, DIC, MeitY.

basicDetails.implementingAgency: Small Farmers Agri Business Consortium

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The "e-National Agriculture Market (e-NAM)" is a pan-India electronic trading platform launched on 14th April 2016 to integrate APMC mandis across the country under the “One Nation One Market” initiative. Implemented by the Small Farmers Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, the platform provides online trading facilities for agricultural commodities. It offers services such as commodity arrival information, quality assaying, e-bidding, and direct e-payment to farmers through a single-window system. The scheme aims to improve transparency, efficiency, and better price discovery in agricultural marketing. In Jammu & Kashmir, 11 mandis have been integrated with the e-NAM platform since May 2020.
schemeContent.benefits_md: > **For Farmers:** - Access to Pan-India Markets through a digital trading platform. - Real-time Price Discovery based on demand and supply. - Transparency in auction and payment processes. - Better Prices through wider buyer participation. - Online Payment directly to farmers' bank accounts. - Free Quality Testing (Assaying) of produce in markets. - Reduced Information Asymmetry—farmers can see prices and make informed decisions. > **For Markets (APMCs/RMCs):** - One-time Grant of up to ₹30 lakh per market for hardware, internet, assaying labs, etc. - Free e-NAM Software is provided with customization for each state. - Support Staff (1 person per market) provided for 1 year at no cost. - Provision to use Cold Storages & Warehouses as market sub-yards. - Infrastructure Support for setting up: 1. e-auction halls. 1. assaying labs. 1. electronic weighbridges. 1. training facilities. > **For State Governments / UTs:** - Eligibility for Central Funding upon adopting key APMC Act reforms: 1. Single trading license for the state. 1. Single-point market fee. 1. Legal provision for e-trading. - Support for Soil Testing Labs (STLs) under related schemes (NMSA/RKVY). - Training, Dispute Resolution Mechanism, and linking more markets to e-NAM.

Registration Guidelines for farmers:
Users can register by Clicking
here
Select “Registration Type” as “Farmer” and select the desired “APMC”.
Provide a valid email ID, as you will receive your Login ID and Password on it.
Once successfully registered, you will receive a login ID and a temporary password at the given email.
Log in to the dashboard by clicking the icon on
www.enam.gov.in/web
You will see a flashing message on the dashboard: “Click here to register with APMC.”
Click on the flashing link, which will redirect you to the registration page for filling or updating details.
Your application will be sent for approval to your selected APMC after KYC is completed.
After successfully logging in to your dashboard, you will be able to see all APMC address details.

After successful submission, the user will receive an email confirming that the application has been submitted to the concerned APMC, with the status shown as Submitted, In Progress, Approved, or Rejected.
Once approved by the APMC, you will receive your eNAM Farmer Permanent Login ID (e.g., HR866F00001) and password for complete access to the e-NAM platform at your registered email address.
Alternatively, you can contact your respective Mandi/APMC for the same.
Registration Guidelines for Trades:
Users will have to register by visiting
http://enam.gov.in/NAMV2/home/other_register.html
Select “Registration Type” as “Trader” and choose the appropriate “APMC” or State Level option.
Provide your passport-size photograph and correct email ID to receive your login ID and password at the same address.
After successful registration, you will receive your login ID and a temporary password at your provided email ID.
Log in to the dashboard by clicking the icon on
www.enam.gov.in
Then you will see a flashing message on the dashboard: “Click here to register with APMC.”
Click on the flashing link, which will redirect you to the registration page for filling or updating details.
Your application will be submitted for approval to your selected APMC or SAMB (in case of a Unified License).
After successfully logging in to your dashboard, you will be able to see the arrivals and trade activities happening in the APMC for notified commodities in eNAM.
You will see a flashing message on the dashboard: “Click on the link.”
It will redirect you to the registration page to submit your license and KYC details as a trader.
Your details will be submitted for approval by your selected APMC.
Once successfully submitted, you will receive an email confirming the status of the application as Submitted, In Progress, Approved, or Rejected.
Its status can be viewed by logging in to the dashboard, as explained earlier.
For a permanent login ID (e.g., HR866T00001) and password, visit your respective Mandi/APMC and verify your license number.
After successful approval by the APMC, eNAM Trader/CA IDs and passwords will be sent to the provided email address.
Trader/CA users can participate in online trade using the provided login ID and password.
For FPOs/FPCs:
FPOs/FPCs can register on e-NAM Portal via the website (
www.enam.gov.in
) or mobile app or provide following details at the nearest e-NAM mandi:
Name of your FPOs/FPCs.
Name, address, email ID, and contact number of the authorized person (MD/CEO/Manager).
Bank account details (Name of bank, branch, account number, IFSC code).
For Mandi Board:
States (State Agricultural Marketing Boards) interested in integrating their mandis with NAM are required to carry out the following reforms in their APMC Act:
Provide for a single (unified) trading license valid across the state.
Implement a single-point levy of market fees across the state.
Include provisions for e-auction/e-trading as modes of price discovery.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md: 1. The applicant State/UT must allow a single trading license valid across the State, issued through suitable legislation or executive orders. - The process should be liberal, without barriers like high deposits, quantity restrictions, or mandatory purchase centers. 1. The applicant State/UT must ensure single-point levy of market fee, applicable only at the first wholesale transaction. - No additional charges should be levied on subsequent wholesale transactions of the same produce. 1. The applicant State/UT must provide legal and infrastructural support for e-auction/e-trading, through relevant amendments or executive provisions. - The applicant must submit proposals in the prescribed format and fulfill all three core reforms above to be eligible for the one-time grant for infrastructure setup (hardware, internet, assaying equipment, etc.). 1. The applicant must commit to: - Trading 100% of selected commodities through e-NAM in the proposed markets. - Providing or linking markets to Soil Testing Laboratories (STLs). - Covering extra implementation costs beyond the sanctioned amount. - Bearing costs of software maintenance after 5 years. - Registering the implementing agency on the PFMS portal and submitting necessary bank details to the Department. 1. The applicant State/UT, if lacking an APMC Act or not enforcing it, must: - Identify an appropriate institution/organization. - Frame enforceable guidelines to enable e-trading, including trader registration, transaction norms, and infrastructure provisioning. 1. The applicant private market, if applying, must: - Be recommended by the concerned authority. - Provide all necessary infrastructure and services (e.g., analyst, assaying facilities) at its own expense.

Step 1:
Preparing the Research Proposal

The applicant must carefully read the guidelines and prepare a comprehensive research proposal stating a synopsis of the work already done, objectives, methodology, estimated cost, duration, milestones, and physical and financial phasing. The estimated cost must be structured into specific expenditure heads, supported by necessary quotations and justifications.
Step 2:
Securing End User Views

The applicant must identify possible end-users for the results of the proposed research. The applicant must then obtain their views and enclose a certificate from at least two such end-users along with the proposal.
Step 3:
Submitting the Application

The Principal Investigator must get the proposal duly recommended and endorsed by the Head of the Institute. The applicant must then submit five physical copies of the proposal along with a soft copy in PDF and Word format to the concerned Indian National Committee secretariat.
Step 4:
Evaluating and Reviewing the Proposal

The Indian National Committee secretariat will examine the proposal, allocate an identification number, and send it to peer reviewers and committee members. The committee may ask the Principal Investigator to submit a revised proposal after incorporating the views of the experts and reviewers.
Step 5:
Approving the Scheme

The applicant will be invited to present the proposal before the committee for discussion. The recommended proposals will be forwarded to the Research And Development Division for administrative approval and a formal sanction order will be issued by the competent authority.
Step 6:
Executing the Bond and Releasing Funds

The Principal Investigator and the Head of the Institution must submit the acceptance of the terms and conditions. Non-Governmental Organizations must execute a prescribed bond with two sureties, after which the Ministry will process the release of the first installment of funds directly into the bank account of the institution.
Application Process Detailing
Where to Apply:

Applications must be sent physically to the Secretariats of the Indian National Committee on Surface Water (Sewa Bhawan, R.K. Puram, New Delhi), the Indian National Committee on Ground Water (Jamnagar House, Mansingh Road, New Delhi), or the Indian National Committee on Climate Change (National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee) depending on the research domain.
Application Deadlines:
The research proposal can be submitted at any time during the year.
Grievance Redressal / Help & Support:

Director, Research And Development Division, Ministry of Water Resources, Wing No. 4, I Floor, West Block No.1, R.K. Puram, New Delhi - 110066. Telephone and Fax: 011-26104082. Email: watrnd-mowr@nic.in.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md: - The applicant must be an academician or expert working in Indian Institutes of Technology, recognized universities, recognized engineering and agricultural colleges, or Water and Land Management Institutes. - The applicant must be an expert from an organization under the Ministry Of Water Resources or from a research and development institute or laboratory of the Central or State Government. - The applicant must be from an Indian Non-Governmental Organization registered under the relevant Society Act. - The applicant must be from a non-profit making recognized Indian Private Research and Development Institution registered with the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research. - The applicant must propose a research topic that falls within the subject domain or priority areas related to the respective Indian National Committee. - The applicant must ensure the proposed research has not been done elsewhere to avoid duplication. - The applicant must identify the probable users of the new technology and end-users of the results of the proposed research. - The applicant must not seek funding for foreign travel, salaries of regular employees of the institute, or honorariums for investigators. - The applicant must not utilize the grant for the construction, maintenance, or repair of buildings, or the purchase of vehicles and air conditioners. - The applicant must complete any previous ongoing research projects funded by the Ministry of Water Resources before a new research proposal can be considered. - The applicant must be an Indian citizen to be eligible for research fellowships and associateships. - The applicant must ensure the upper age limit for Junior Research Fellow, Senior Research Fellow, and Research Associate is 28, 32, and 35 years respectively on the day of application. ##### ***Desirable Criteria*** The applicant should associate a Co-Principal Investigator in the research scheme. ##### ***Post-Selection Conditions*** - The applicant must execute a bond with two sureties to the President of India if applying as a Non-Governmental Organization. - The applicant must maintain a separate audited account and register for permanent or semi-permanent assets acquired solely out of the project grant. - The applicant must publish research papers emerging out of the research scheme in leading journals with prior approval of the Ministry of Water Resources. - The applicant must acknowledge the assistance received from the funding agency in all publications and patent findings. ##### ***Relaxation*** The applicant should note that the upper age limit for fellowships is relaxable for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Other Backward Classes, Women, and physically handicapped candidates.

schemeContent.briefDescription: The scheme aims to propagate and develop literature in the field of law in Hindi and other regional languages. It provides financial grants to voluntary organisations for publishing legal books, commentaries, and journals.
schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The scheme "Assistance to Voluntary Organisations for Promotion of the Official Languages in the Field of Law" was launched by the Legislative Department, Government Of India. The scheme aims to propagate and develop literature in the field of law in Hindi and other regional languages. The scheme provides financial assistance covering up to 85% of the anticipated net expenditure for producing legal literature, such as commentaries, treatises, and law journals. The applicant must be a voluntary organisation undertaking activities conducive to the enrichment and use of Official Languages in the legal field. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry Of Law And Justice. The applications for this scheme are accepted offline via submission to the Official Languages Wing at Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi.

_If the organisation ceases to exist, the equipment purchased out of the central grant will revert to the Government of India._ - _The accounts of the organisation must be properly maintained and submitted as required for checking by the Legislative Department or Indian Audit And Accounts Department._ - _The organisation must exercise the utmost economy in its working._ - _The grant must be utilized strictly for the purpose for which it was sanctioned._ - _Progress reports about the project must be furnished at regular intervals._ - _An audited statement of expenditure and a report on the work done must be furnished immediately after the completion of the project or before drawing a subsequent installment._ - _The organisation must submit a Utilisation Certificate in respect of the grant received during the preceding year._ - _Such number of copies, not exceeding five, of all publications brought out with central assistance must be supplied to the Legislative Department free of cost._ - _The organisation must maintain an audited record of the assets acquired or created wholly or substantially with the help of the grant in the prescribed proforma._ - _The author of a published book must use the Hindi legal terms occurring in the authoritative texts of the Central Acts, State Acts, or the Legal Glossary published by the Official Languages Wing._ - _The organisation must give an undertaking to complete the project within a reasonable time fixed by the Government._

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The "INSPIRE FACULTY FELLOWSHIP" component provides opportunities to 100 persons every year with Ph.D. qualifications in the age group of 27-32 years for 5 years to carry out research in both basic and applied science areas including engineering, medicine, agriculture, and veterinary sciences for establishing themselves as independent researchers. It grants an attractive fellowship for a duration of 5 years. The objective of the scheme is to encourage young researchers to continue research in areas of S&T, Medicine, Agriculture, Pharmacy, and Veterinary Sciences. Purpose 1. To provide attractive opportunities for young achievers for developing independent scientific profiles and launch them toward fulfilling long-term careers. 2. To augment high-quality scientific manpower in scientific and educational institutions, especially the Central and State universities. 3. While vertical migration from the other INSPIRE components would be encouraged, the faculty fellowship component also provides the opportunity to meritorious candidates for lateral entry into INSPIRE scheme. 4. INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship provides an opportunity to post-doctoral fellows for carrying out independent research however does not guarantee a regular position after 5 years.
schemeContent.benefits_md: > **Amount** 1. Each selected INSPIRE Faculty Fellow will be eligible to receive a consolidated amount of ₹1,25,000/- per month as a fellowship with an annual increment of ₹2,000/-. 1. In addition, a Research Grant of ₹7,00,000 every year for 5 years will also be provided to each successful candidate including the carry-forward amount, if any, from the previous year. 1. The consolidated amount of ₹1,25,000/- per month is an all-inclusive fellowship and taxable as per the Indian IT Act. > **Duration** 1. The INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship is for a maximum period of 5 (five) years.

basicDetails.schemeName: Ecomark Scheme of India (ECOMARK)

nodalMinistryName.label: Ministry Of Environment,forests and climate change

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The scheme "Ecomark Scheme of India (ECOMARK)" was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The scheme provides an "Ecomark" label for products that meet specified environmental criteria with respect to resource consumption and environmental impacts, enabling consumers to make informed purchase decisions. The applicant must submit an application for the grant of Ecomark to the Central Pollution Control Board in Form 1. The scheme is implemented by the Central Pollution Control Board. The applications for this scheme are accepted online through the Ecomark web portal.
schemeContent.benefits_md: - The scheme grants an Ecomark label to the product. - The Ecomark granted to the product shall be valid for a period of three years or until a change in the Ecomark criteria for the product, whichever is earlier. ##### ***Conditions*** - Every holder of Ecomark shall submit an annual report to the Central Pollution Control Board online through the web portal on or before the 31st May of every year. - Every person who has been granted an Ecomark in respect of a product shall affix on such product an Ecomark label granted under these rules. - The holder of Ecomark shall allow the Central Pollution Control Board or the registered agencies to undertake such inspection and verification as may be considered necessary for ensuring compliance. - The holder of the Ecomark shall grant access to the premises in which the product concerned is produced or kept to the Central Pollution Control Board and the registered agency.
schemeContent.briefDescription: The scheme aims to encourage the demand for environment-friendly products that cause lesser adverse impacts on the environment. Accessing the Ecomark Portal
The applicant must access the
centralized online Ecomark web portal
developed by the Central Pollution Control Board for making applications and tracking Ecomark certification.
Step 2:
Submitting the Application Form
The applicant must fill and submit an application for the grant of Ecomark for a product which complies with the specified conditions to the Central Pollution Control Board.
Step 3:
Verification of the Product
On receipt of the application, the Central Pollution Control Board shall, by itself or through a designated Verifier, verify whether the product complies with the required environmental conditions.
Step 4:
Preparation and Submission of the Report
After making such verification, the Central Pollution Control Board or the Verifier shall prepare a report and submit it within a period of sixty days from the date of such verification.
Step 5:
Grant of the Ecomark Certificate
On receipt of the verification report, if the Central Pollution Control Board is satisfied that the product complies with the conditions, it may grant the Ecomark to the product.

basicDetails.schemeName: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The "Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)" is one of the five sub-schemes of the National Social Assistance Programme, Ministry of Rural Development. Under this scheme, persons belonging to BPL households and 60 years or above in age are eligible to apply. This program is being implemented in rural areas as well as urban areas. The Government of India, on 15th August 1995, introduced the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) as a fully funded Centrally Sponsored Scheme targeting the destitute, defined as any person who has little or no regular means of subsistence from his/her own source of income or through financial support from family members or other sources. > **The NSAP at present includes five sub-schemes as its components-** a) Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) b) Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) c) Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) d) National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) e) Annapurna Scheme > **Objectives of NSAP-** 1. Provides social assistance benefits to poor households in the case of death, maternity, or old age of the breadwinner. 2. Ensure minimum national standards, in addition to the benefits that the states are currently providing or might provide in the future. 3. Ensure uniform social protection for the beneficiaries across the country without interruption. > **Expansion to cover all eligible BPL persons-** In 2007, the scheme was expanded to cover all eligible persons Below Poverty Line (BPL).
schemeContent.benefits_md: - ₹200 per month for beneficiaries aged 60–79 years. - ₹500 per month for beneficiaries aged 80 years and above. > **Note:** At present old age beneficiaries are getting anywhere between ₹200/- to ₹1000/- depending on the State Contribution.

nodalMinistryName.label: Ministry of Women and Child Development

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The scheme “Mission Vatsalya (Child Protection Services and Child Welfare Services)” is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India. The scheme aims to strengthen child protection mechanisms and ensure the care, protection, development, and well-being of children. It promotes family- and community-based care, institutional support services, counselling, and emergency outreach for children in need. The scheme also focuses on safeguarding children from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and vulnerabilities through coordinated efforts at national, state, district, and community levels. It encourages awareness generation, capacity building, and participation of local bodies and communities for effective child welfare and protection services.
schemeContent.benefits_md: > **Financial Support for Vulnerable Children:** - Children living with biological parents or extended families receive financial assistance to meet their education, nutrition, and healthcare needs, helping prevent separation from families. > **Family-Based Foster Care Support:** - Children without parental care are placed with biologically unrelated foster families, ensuring a nurturing home environment. Foster parents receive financial assistance to support the child’s care, protection, and rehabilitation. > **Legal and Safe Adoption Opportunities:** - Children declared legally free for adoption are placed in permanent family settings through Specialised Adoption Agencies (SAAs), ensuring their long-term emotional and social well-being. > **After-Care Support for Independent Living:** - Children exiting Child Care Institutions at the age of 18 are provided financial assistance up to 21 years, extendable to 23 years, to support education, skill development, employment, and smooth reintegration into society. > **Monthly Financial Assistance:** - A monthly grant of ₹4,000 per child is provided to State Governments under Sponsorship, Foster Care, or After-Care to ensure sustained support. > **Strengthened Child Protection Systems:** - State Governments are encouraged to provide additional grants and proactively identify children in need of care and protection with the support of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and Urban Local Bodies. > **Transparent Approval and Monitoring Mechanism:** - Every district establishes a Sponsorship and Foster Care Approval Committee (SFCAC) to review, approve, and sanction assistance, ensuring accountability and timely support. > **Compliance with Legal Framework:** - All non-institutional care interventions are implemented in accordance with the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act and Rules, ensuring legality, safety, and child-centric care.
schemeContent.briefDescription: This scheme aims to ensure, sustain, and strengthen child protection at the family and community levels, promote family-based non-institutional care, and provide financial support to children in need.

children.text: The scheme “Mission Vatsalya (Child Protection Services and Child Welfare Services)” is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India. The scheme aims to strengthen child protection mechanisms and ensure the care, protection, development, and well-being of children. It promotes family- and community-based care, institutional support services, counselling, and emergency outreach for children in need. The scheme also focuses on safeguarding children from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and vulnerabilities through coordinated efforts at national, state, district, and community levels. It encourages awareness generation, capacity building, and participation of local bodies and communities for effective child welfare and protection services.
Financial Support for Vulnerable Children:
Children living with biological parents or extended families receive financial assistance to meet their education, nutrition, and healthcare needs, helping prevent separation from families.
Family-Based Foster Care Support:

Children without parental care are placed with biologically unrelated foster families, ensuring a nurturing home environment. Foster parents receive financial assistance to support the child’s care, protection, and rehabilitation.
Legal and Safe Adoption Opportunities:
Children declared legally free for adoption are placed in permanent family settings through Specialised Adoption Agencies (SAAs), ensuring their long-term emotional and social well-being.
After-Care Support for Independent Living:

Children exiting Child Care Institutions at the age of 18 are provided financial assistance up to 21 years, extendable to 23 years, to support education, skill development, employment, and smooth reintegration into society.
Monthly Financial Assistance:
A monthly grant of ₹4,000 per child is provided to State Governments under Sponsorship, Foster Care, or After-Care to ensure sustained support.
Strengthened Child Protection Systems:

State Governments are encouraged to provide additional grants and proactively identify children in need of care and protection with the support of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and Urban Local Bodies.
Transparent Approval and Monitoring Mechanism:
Every district establishes a Sponsorship and Foster Care Approval Committee (SFCAC) to review, approve, and sanction assistance, ensuring accountability and timely support.
Compliance with Legal Framework:
All non-institutional care interventions are implemented in accordance with the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act and Rules, ensuring legality, safety, and child-centric care.

basicDetails.schemeName: AFFDF-Financial Assistance For Treatment Of Serious Diseases To Non Pensioner Ex-Servicemen (All Ranks)/Widows

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The scheme "Financial Assistance for Treatment of Serious Diseases to Non-Pensioner Ex-Servicemen (ESM) (All Ranks)/Widows" is implemented by the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare, Ministry of Defence, Government of India to provide financial assistance for the treatment of approved serious diseases to non-pensioner Ex-Servicemen and widows. The scheme supports expenditure incurred on hospitalization, medicines, and medical treatment for specified serious diseases. Assistance is provided subject to prescribed limits and eligibility conditions. Applications are processed through the Zila Sainik Board and approved by the Kendriya Sainik Board. The approved amount is transferred directly to the beneficiary's bank account through Electronic Clearance Service (ECS).
schemeContent.benefits_md: > **For Non-Pensioner Officers/Widows:** - **Medical Treatment Assistance:** Financial assistance of 75% of the total expenditure incurred on medical treatment, hospitalization, medicines, and related expenses.- **Maximum Assistance Limit:** Maximum financial assistance of ₹1,50,000/- (one-time) for approved serious diseases.- **Cancer Treatment and Dialysis Assistance:** Financial assistance of up to ₹75,000/- per annum for cancer treatment and dialysis. > **For Non-Pensioner Other Ranks/Widows:** - **Medical Treatment Assistance:** Financial assistance of 90% of the total expenditure incurred on medical treatment, hospitalization, medicines, and related expenses.- **Maximum Assistance Limit:** Maximum financial assistance of ₹1,50,000/- (one-time) for approved serious diseases.- **Cancer Treatment and Dialysis Assistance:** Financial assistance of up to ₹75,000/- per annum for cancer treatment and dialysis. > **List of the serious diseases are covered under this scheme:-** 1. Angiography & Angioplasty 1. CABG. (l) Dialysis 1. Open heart surgery 1. Valve replacement 1. Pacemaker Implant 1. Cerebral stroke 1. Prostrate surgery 1. Joint replacement 1. Renal failure 1. Cancer > **Treatment of other Diseases:** - In case the treatment of a serious disease which is not listed in this scheme-document, such application will be referred to DGAFMS for comment/recommendation to consider it for financial assistance for treatment of that disease, to ESM under this scheme. > **Note:** - Expenditure must be incurred at an approved govt hospital at the rates applicable under CGHS / ECHS.
schemeContent.briefDescription: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to non-pensioner Ex-Servicemen of all ranks and widows for meeting medical expenses incurred on the treatment of approved serious diseases, including cancer, renal failure, knee replacement, and heart surgery.

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The "ICAR Emeritus Scientist" scheme is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare to utilize the services of outstanding superannuated scientists for completing nationally important research work and contributing to agricultural education and development. The scheme supports retired scientists in continuing ongoing research projects of national importance and participating in specialized teaching programmes. It also promotes the development of instructional materials and addresses policy issues related to agriculture and allied sciences. The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of honorarium, contingency grants, and support for research personnel. The appointment is granted for a fixed tenure of 3 years without extension.
schemeContent.benefits_md: > **Honorarium:** - ₹50,000/- per month honorarium in addition to pension. - Subject to provisions of the Income Tax Act. > **Contingency Grant:** - Up to ₹2,00,000/- per annum per scientist. - Used for chemicals, glassware, books, stationery, laboratory assistance, and ministerial help. - May be enhanced with approval based on the nature of research work. - Can be used for domestic travel related to research, data collection, scientific meetings, conferences, and ICAR review meetings. - Includes economy-class airfare, eligible daily allowance, and road mileage within India. > **Research Personnel Support:** - Financial assistance for engagement of: - Junior Research Fellow (JRF) - Senior Research Fellow (SRF) - Research Associate (RA) - Appointment remains valid until completion of the project. > **Leave Benefits:** - 1 month leave with honorarium for each completed year of tenure. - Leave on a pro-rata basis for any fraction of a year. - Up to 3 months leave without honorarium may be granted on health grounds with a medical certificate. > **Research and Academic Support:** - Opportunity to complete ongoing nationally important research. - Opportunity to teach specialized courses in universities and institutions. - Opportunity to develop instructional and multimedia educational materials.
schemeContent.briefDescription: The scheme aims to utilize the expertise of outstanding superannuated scientists of the National Agricultural Research System by supporting nationally important research, teaching, human resource development, and extension activities through honorarium and research grants.

Step 1:
Obtain and fill out the prescribed
application proforma
for the ICAR Emeritus Scientist Scheme.
Step 2:
Prepare the project proposal and attach all required supporting documents.
Step 3:
Submit the completed application to the Executive Authority of the institution where the proposed research, teaching, human resource development, or extension work will be carried out.
Step 4:
Obtain recommendation and justification from the Executive Authority. Only applications forwarded through the Executive Authority will be considered.
Step 5:
Email the duly recommended application to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com.
Step 6:
Mention "Application for Emeritus Scientist Scheme – Name of Applicant – Contact Number" in the subject line of the email.
Step 7:
Ensure that the application is submitted on or before 30 March 2026.
Step 8:
The submitted application will be scrutinised and considered for selection as per the scheme guidelines.
Procedure of Selection:

The applications received will be referred to the concerned Subject Matter Division of ICAR and to a  specialist in the discipline of the applicant for comments.  The applications along with these comments will be placed before the Selection cum Standing Committee.
Following criteria will be  taken into  consideration  for the selection  of an Emeritus Scientist:

The scientist should have a minimum of 5 research papers in refereed journals in the last five years or should have received a national/ international level award/recognition or in case of teachers must have received national/university level awards for excellence in teaching or have received a letter of appreciation for excellence in teaching based on alumni feedback.
The project proposal is of national importance and other equally competent regular scientists are not available in the institute to carry out the proposed work.
The project proposal is in continuation of his/her work.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md: - The applicant must be a scientist of repute from the National Agricultural Research System (NARS). - The applicant must hold or have held the position of Principal Scientist, Professor, or above in an eligible institution. - The applicant must be retiring within the next 12 months or must have retired within 1 year from the last working day of the notification month. - The applicant must not be more than 65 years of age at the time of application. - The applicant must have at least 5 research papers published in refereed journals during the last 5 years, or must have received a national/international award or recognition. - In the case of teachers, the applicant must have received a teaching excellence award or appreciation for outstanding teaching performance. - The applicant must submit a project of national importance that is a continuation of his/her previous work. - The applicant must demonstrate that an equally competent regular scientist is not available in the institution to undertake the proposed work. - The applicant must be willing to devote full time to the approved project and must not accept any other remunerative employment during the tenure. - The applicant must not receive financial assistance for the same work from any other source while availing benefits under this scheme.

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The "ICAR Emeritus Professor Scheme" is implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, to utilise the expertise and services of outstanding superannuated teachers and scientists from the National Agricultural Research and Education System (NARES). The scheme provides an opportunity to retired professionals to undertake teaching, training, student research guidance, and other academic activities in agricultural universities and institutions. It supports the development of instructional materials, textbooks, and e-learning resources for use in national agricultural education programmes and distance education. The scheme aims to address shortages in faculty positions, strengthen agricultural education, and leverage the experience of retired experts in addressing nationally important academic and policy issues. It also encourages retired teachers and scientists to contribute to higher agricultural education, particularly in economically and ecologically underprivileged regions.
schemeContent.benefits_md: > **Honorarium:** - Honorarium of ₹50,000/- per month is provided to the Emeritus Professor. > **Contingency Grant:** - A non-lapsable contingency grant of ₹1,00,000/- per annum is provided. - The grant may be used for secretarial assistance, stationery, postage, consumables, books, journals, and travel related to the approved assignment. - The grant may also be used for attending one scientific meeting or conference within India per year. - Economy-class airfare, admissible daily allowance, and road mileage are allowed from the contingency grant. - No separate Travel Allowance (TA) or Daily Allowance (DA) is provided. - The grant is released based on requisition and actual utilization of the previous year's grant. - Books and journals purchased from the grant become the property of the concerned university or college. - The contingency grant may be enhanced with the concurrence of the Financial Adviser (Department of Agricultural Research and Education), depending on the assignment. > **Academic and Institutional Support:** - The Emeritus Professor is entitled to medical and other facilities available to university faculty members. - The Emeritus Professor remains attached to an Agricultural University, ICAR Deemed University, or another eligible institution that provides the required facilities. > **Research and Professional Engagement** - The Emeritus Professor is provided an opportunity to continue approved academic, research, and professional activities in agriculture and allied sciences.

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The RMEWF – Financial Assistance for Medical Treatment of Ex-Servicemen scheme is implemented by the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare, Ministry of Defence, Government of India.All the pensioners of Armed Forces have been provided medical cover compulsorily under ECHS wef 01 Apr 2008. However, non-pensioner ESM who were sent out of services early in their life due to organizational constraints or discharged at their own request have no such medical cover. With ever increasing costs of health care, it becomes extremely difficult for non-pensioner ESM to combat diseases especially in old age. At such age, medical expenses push such ESM into a state of poverty and loss of dignity. The scheme to provide financial assistance to non-pensioners, who are without any other sources of income and in state of penury,was started in year 1981 with an amount depending upon nature and gravity of ailment. This was last revised in August 2023 with onetime grant of Rs 50,000/-. **Aim** The aim of this aid gratis is to provide financial assistance to non-pensioner ESM or their widow to meet routine medical expenses during the year.

schemeContent.briefDescription: To motivate the pepper growers to produce good quality pepper for export by promoting installation of pepper threshers for hygienic separation of pepper berries from the spikes.

basicDetails.schemeName: NIDHI – Seed Support Program (SSP)

schemeContent.briefDescription: The key objective of the NIDHI- Seed Support Program (NIDHI-SSP) is to ensure availability of the seed support through incubators for providing timely support to potential startups, thereby enabling them to take their ventures to the next level and facilitate their success in the marketplace.
schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The NIDHI Seed Support Program (NIDHI-SSP) is implemented by the Department of Science and Technology under the Ministry of Science and Technology. The Scheme is designed to provide timely financial assistance to the incubators to support potential startups with promising ideas, innovations and technologies. The key objective of the NIDHI- Seed Support Program (NIDHI-SSP) is to ensure availability of the seed support through incubators for providing timely support to potential startups, thereby enabling them to take their ventures to the next level and facilitate their success in the marketplace. The scheme also enables the incubators to widen their pipeline of startups and also share the success of their startups which would also result in ensuring their long term operational sustainability. This seed support is intended to act as a bridge between the development and commercialization of innovative technologies, products, and services, and to facilitate the success of incubatee startups in a relatively hassle-free manner.
schemeContent.benefits_md: **For Incubators/TBIs:** The maximum financial support that will be made available to an incubator is INR 1000 lakh, which will be released in phases according to the needs, capacity, and capabilities of the incubator, following a proper process. **For Startups/Entrepreneurs:** The maximum support that will be given to a deserving startup is up to INR 100 lakh. This support will be provided to help startups get off the ground and grow, increasing their chances of success in the marketplace.

nodalMinistryName.label: Ministry Of Skill Development And Entrepreneurship

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The scheme "Skill Loan Scheme" by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, aims to support youth who wish to undergo skill training programmes in the country and ensure access to institutional credit for pursuing skill courses. Through this scheme, collateral-free loans without third-party guarantee and credit guarantee support are provided to eligible borrowers for undertaking skill training courses, including higher-end, fee-based skilling courses for new-age skills. The scheme is implemented through eligible lending institutions, including Scheduled Banks, Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), and Non-Banking Finance Company Micro Finance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs). **Objectives:** - To support youth seeking skill training opportunities in the country. - To ensure access to institutional credit for pursuing skill courses.
schemeContent.benefits_md: 1. The maximum loan limit under the Scheme has been enhanced from ₹1,50,000 to ₹7,50,000. 1. The minimum and maximum loan limit under the Scheme are ₹5,000 and ₹7,50,000 respectively. 1. The loan is provided without any collateral security and/or third-party guarantee. 1. Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and Non-Banking Finance Company Micro Finance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs) have been included as eligible lending institutions in addition to Scheduled Banks under the Scheme. 1. The interest rate charged by Member Lending Institutions should not be more than: - 1.5% per annum over External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) for Scheduled Banks. - 21% per annum for NBFC/NBFC-MFIs. 1. The Scheme provides guarantee cover to the extent of 70% to 75% of the amount in default. 1. The claim payout to an eligible Lending Institution during the initial years is capped at 20% of the total disbursement made by the institution under the Scheme during a year. 1. basicDetails.schemeName: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer-2021, effective from January 27, 2022, is a crucial initiative led by the Ministry of Labour &amp; Employment, Government of India that addresses eradicating bonded labour in India. It introduces varying rehabilitation assistance amounts based on beneficiary categories, such as adults, children, women, and extreme cases, with provisions for annuity schemes and Direct Benefit Transfer. The scheme also facilitates surveys, awareness programs, and evaluatory studies to combat bonded labour, with financial support. It emphasizes skill development, socio-economic assistance, and monitoring mechanisms, all aimed at offering comprehensive support to eradicate the bonded labour system in the country.
schemeContent.benefits_md:
> **For Adult Male Beneficiaries** - The rehabilitation assistance shall be ₹1,00,000/- per adult male beneficiary. - Beneficiaries have the option to deposit the assistance in an annuity scheme or receive it as a cash grant. - The District Administration will assess the cash requirement of the beneficiary and, with their consent, place the money in an annuity scheme.
> **Special Category Beneficiaries (Children, Women)** - Rehabilitation assistance for special category beneficiaries, such as children, including orphans, or those rescued from forced labour, and women, shall be ₹2,00,000/-. - At least ₹1,25,000/- shall be deposited in an annuity scheme in each beneficiary's name. - The remaining amount shall be transferred to the beneficiary's account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
> **Extreme Cases of Bonded or Forced Labor** - In cases of extreme deprivation, such as transgender individuals, women, and children rescued from sexual exploitation, or trafficking, the rehabilitation assistance shall be ₹3,00,000/-. - At least ₹2,00,000/- shall be deposited in an annuity scheme in each beneficiary's name. - ₹1,00,000/- shall be transferred to the beneficiary's account via DBT.
> **Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund** - Each state shall create a Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund at the district level with a permanent corpus of at least ₹10,00,000 (Ten Lakhs Rupees) at the disposal of the District Magistrate. - Penalties recovered from convicted perpetrators of bonded labour may be deposited in this corpus.
> **Immediate Financial Assistance** - The District Administration shall provide immediate financial assistance up to ₹30,000/- to rescued individuals from the District Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund. - The District Magistrate may disburse higher amounts if required but limited to the maximum entitlement prescribed under this scheme.
> **State Government Responsibilities** - Providing a safe and secure environment for capacity building of child-bonded labourers. - Addressing the special needs of female freed bonded labourers, including financial support for marriage. - Offering special care for disabled individuals, in line with the national policy for disabled people. - Providing employable skill development training for adult bonded labourers who do not fall into the above categories.

children.text: The Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer-2021, effective from January 27, 2022, is a crucial initiative led by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India that addresses eradicating bonded labour in India. It introduces varying rehabilitation assistance amounts based on beneficiary categories, such as adults, children, women, and extreme cases, with provisions for annuity schemes and Direct Benefit Transfer. The scheme also facilitates surveys, awareness programs, and evaluatory studies to combat bonded labour, with financial support. It emphasizes skill development, socio-economic assistance, and monitoring mechanisms, all aimed at offering comprehensive support to eradicate the bonded labour system in the country.
For Adult Male Beneficiaries
The rehabilitation assistance shall be ₹1,00,000/- per adult male beneficiary.
Beneficiaries have the option to deposit the assistance in an annuity scheme or receive it as a cash grant.
The District Administration will assess the cash requirement of the beneficiary and, with their consent, place the money in an annuity scheme.
Special Category Beneficiaries (Children, Women)
Rehabilitation assistance for special category beneficiaries, such as children, including orphans, or those rescued from forced labour, and women, shall be ₹2,00,000/-.
At least ₹1,25,000/- shall be deposited in an annuity scheme in each beneficiary's name.
The remaining amount shall be transferred to the beneficiary's account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
Extreme Cases of Bonded or Forced Labor
In cases of extreme deprivation, such as transgender individuals, women, and children rescued from sexual exploitation, or trafficking, the rehabilitation assistance shall be ₹3,00,000/-.
At least ₹2,00,000/- shall be deposited in an annuity scheme in each beneficiary's name.
₹1,00,000/- shall be transferred to the beneficiary's account via DBT.
Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund
Each state shall create a Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund at the district level with a permanent corpus of at least ₹10,00,000 (Ten Lakhs Rupees) at the disposal of the District Magistrate.
Penalties recovered from convicted perpetrators of bonded labour may be deposited in this corpus.
Immediate Financial Assistance
The District Administration shall provide immediate financial assistance up to ₹30,000/- to rescued individuals from the District Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund.
The District Magistrate may disburse higher amounts if required but limited to the maximum entitlement prescribed under this scheme.
State Government Responsibilities
Providing a safe and secure environment for capacity building of child-bonded labourers.
Addressing the special needs of female freed bonded labourers, including financial support for marriage.
Offering special care for disabled individuals, in line with the national policy for disabled people.
Providing employable skill development training for adult bonded labourers who do not fall into the above categories.

schemeContent.briefDescription: The scheme aims to provide standardized world-class Bed & Breakfast accommodation facilities, supplement tourist accommodation, and promote clean, affordable, and homely stays for domestic and foreign tourists in States and Union Territories where no State/UT approval scheme exists.
schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The "Incredible India Bed & Breakfast Establishments" scheme implemented by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, aims to provide standardized world-class Bed & Breakfast accommodation by classifying eligible establishments in States and Union Territories where no State or Union Territory approval or accreditation scheme exists. The scheme promotes clean, affordable, and homely accommodation for domestic and foreign tourists while encouraging them to experience Indian traditions and hospitality. Eligible establishments are classified under Silver and Gold categories after inspection by the Regional Classification Committee. Approved establishments are publicized by the Ministry of Tourism and included in an official directory, and hospitality training may also be organized for interested operators.
schemeContent.benefits_md: - **Standardized Classification:** Eligible establishments receive classification as Silver or Gold category. - **Official Recognition:** Approved establishments are recognized by the Ministry of Tourism. - **Publicity:** Approved establishments are publicized by the Ministry of Tourism. These are also included in the official directory for tourists. - **Hospitality Training:** Interested operators may receive short-term hospitality training. - **Tourist Promotion:** The scheme promotes domestic and international tourism through quality accommodation.

basicDetails.schemeName: NIDHI – Promoting and Accelerating Young and Aspiring Innovators and Startups (PRAYAS)

schemeContent.briefDescription: The scheme provides early-stage funding to support idea validation and proof of concept for technology-based and deep-tech innovations through PRAYAS Centres (PCs) and Advance PRAYAS Centres (APCs).
schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: NIDHI – Promoting and Accelerating Young and Aspiring Innovators and Startups (PRAYAS) is a scheme of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India. The scheme supports young innovators and startups in transforming innovative ideas into prototypes or proof of concept (PoC) by providing financial assistance of up to ₹10 lakh. It also offers access to incubation infrastructure, mentorship, technical and financial guidance, and industry linkages through Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) and PRAYAS Shalas (Fab Labs). The scheme aims to promote indigenous innovation, technology-based entrepreneurship, and the development of commercially viable products in line with the Atmanirbhar Bharat Mission. **Objectives** **The objectives of NIDHI – PRAYAS are :-** - To enable translation of an innovative idea to a prototype. - To provide a platform for faster experimentation and modify approaches in the idea to market journey. - To indigenously generate innovative solutions relevant to the local and global problems. - To attract a large number of youth who demonstrate problem solving zeal and abilities to work on their new technology/knowledge/innovation-based startups. - To enhance the pipeline in terms of quality and quantity of innovative start ups to the incubators. To build a vibrant innovation ecosystem, by establishing a network between innovators, academia, mentors and incubators.
schemeContent.benefits_md: • Level 1 – PCs: Each innovator/startup supported by a Level 1 Centre PC may receive up to ₹20 Lakhs grant for prototyping. DST provides up to ₹2 crore per annum to each PC. • Level 2 – APCs: Provides prototyping grants of up to ₹40 lakh per innovator/ startup. DST provides up to ₹4 crore per annum to each APC.

basicDetails.schemeName: Global Engagement Scheme: Grant-In-Aid To Indo-Foreign Friendship Cultural Societies

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The scheme "Global Engagement Scheme: Grant-In-Aid To Indo-Foreign Friendship Cultural Societies" component of the Global Engagement Scheme by the ICR Division, Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to generate greater understanding of India's culture and foster closer friendship with people of other countries. Through this component, financial grants are provided to Indo-Foreign Friendship/Cultural Societies actively functioning in foreign countries. The component is implemented by the Ministry of Culture through Indian Missions abroad, with grants authorised via the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and proposals examined by an Expert Committee. > **Objectives:** - Generate greater understanding of India's culture. - Foster closer friendship with people of other countries. - Promote interaction between eminent Indian scholars and their foreign counterparts through holding of seminars on related topics.
schemeContent.benefits_md:
> **Activities for which the Grant is given to the Cultural Societies recommended by the Indian Mission:** Grants under the scheme will be given primarily to cover expenses of the grantees on activities which help projection of India's cultural image and generation of greater understanding of its cultural heritage, and for promoting bilateral cultural contacts by organising the following: - Dance (classical, folk and workshops). - Music (vocal, instrumental, Sufi, classical, semi-classical, Carnatic, contemporary, workshops, etc.). - Photo Exhibitions on culture-related topics. - Exhibitions on Books and other culture-related topics/material. - Publication of Books/journals on culture. - Promotion of Hindi and other Indian languages by organising activities like Workshops, Essay Competition, Dictation and Valedictory Session, Kavi Sammelan and publication of a regional language magazine, etc. - Furnishing the premises of societies having adequate space with replicas of exhibits sourced from the Indian Mission in lieu of cash grant. - Visual Arts and Crafts such as such ceramics, drawing, painting, sculpture, etc. - Contemporary and Modern/Fine Art exhibitions. - Theatre: Drama, Skit, Mime, Mimicry and workshops. - Activities to promote Folk Arts viz Mehendi, Puppetry and Rangoli. - Classes/Courses in Yoga art. - Organisation of Literary events like Debate, Elocution, Creative Writing workshops, Book reading sessions, etc. - Organisation of lecture-demonstrations, seminars, symposiums and conferences on culture-related topics. - Discussions on Indian culture, history, civilisation by inviting eminent scholars, artists, etc. who are interested in Indian affairs can be sponsored. - Promoting interaction between distinguished visiting Indian academics, artists etc with their local counterparts, etc. - Celebrations of Indian festivals - Celebration of National days like India's Republic Day, International Day of Yoga, Indian Independence Day, Hindi Diwas, Gandhi Jayanti, etc. - Celebrations of Anniversaries and centenaries of great Indian personalities and other commemorations of National importance. In this regard, the following activities may be organised. - Organise plays on the theme - Use the theme for activities planned for National Days. - The Works of the personality be translated into major world languages and - Digital Library promotion through Indian Embassies. - Kavi Sammelans in regional languages. - Indian Vegetarian Food Festival to be organised by Indian Embassies abroad. - Commemorative postage stamp on Gandhi to be released. VII. Release of Commemorative coin. - Exhibitions of paintings, rare photographs, books, sculptures, artefacts. - National/International seminars, workshops, competitions, lectures. - Illumination of iconic buildings. > **Please Note:** This Scheme does not grant any funds for operational/ maintenance/capital creation cost of the societies.
> **Amount of Grant:** - The grant shall not ordinarily exceed ₹10,00,000/- (ten lakh) per annum per society. - There is no limit specified on funds authorised to the Mission, as this depends on the funds the Mission can utilise for cultural promotion as per the available number of societies. - An additional amount over and above the maximum limit, up to ₹25,00,000/- (twenty-five lakh), may be granted at the discretion of the Secretary (Culture) in consultation with the Financial Adviser (Culture), where the Ministry proposes to organise the Festival of India/culture weeks to enable expenditure towards hosting cultural troupes, etc.
schemeContent.exclusions_md: 1. The scheme does not grant funds for operational, maintenance, or capital creation costs of the societies. 1. The applicant should not have been sanctioned grant-in-aid for the same activity/purpose from any other source. 1. No other bill for the same purpose and instalment should have already been paid earlier to the grantee. 1. The applicant (society) should not indulge in activities which are sectarian in nature. 1. Grants should normally be utilised for the activities of the society, and not for the direct activities of the Missions.

The Indian Mission ensures the society meets eligibility criteria that it is actively engaged in fostering friendly relations and projecting India's culture, has a well-planned programme of activities, and has gainfully utilised any earlier grant.

The Mission compiles and submits the proposal, comprising Details of the Society (Annexure A), Plan of Activities for the Current Financial Year (Annexure B), Certificate of No Corrupt Practices (Annexure C), Certificate of No Sectarian Activities (Annexure D), and the Utilisation Certificate (GFR 12-A) for any grant last sanctioned.

The Expert Committee, chaired by the Bureau Head In-charge of the ICR Division, with members from IFD, ICCR, and Sangeet Natak Akademi, and convened by the Director/DS (ICR), examines the proposal and recommends the quantum of grant for each society.

The competent authority sanctions the grant to the Bureau Head In-charge of the concerned Division for amounts up to ₹10,00,000/-, or, at the discretion of the Secretary (Culture) in consultation with the Financial Adviser (Culture), up to ₹25,00,000/- in special cases relating to Festival of India/culture weeks.
The grant is issued as an authorisation to the Indian Mission through the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and the amount is placed with the Mission in their accounts.
The Mission informally checks the accounts of the grantee to satisfy itself that the grant has been properly utilised.

After utilising the grant, the society/Mission furnishes the Event Review Report (Annexure E) and a performance-cum-achievement report (2 copies) to the Ministry; video/photo/newspaper clips/audio material may be sent to icr-culture@nic.in and icrculture@gmail.com.
Any unspent balance with the grantee is surrendered to the Government without delay.

basicDetails.schemeName: Research, Development & Innovation (RDI) Scheme

schemeContent.briefDescription: The Research, Development & Innovation (RDI) Scheme provides funding and support to help organizations create and improve new technologies or ideas so they can boost innovation, economic growth, and global competitiveness.
schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: Research, Development & Innovation (RDI) Scheme is a flagship initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India. **OBJECTIVES** • DST has launched the Research, Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, approved by the Cabinet on 1st July 2025, with a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore. • The initiative aims to catalyze private sector participation in high-impact R&D and strengthen India’s capabilities in strategic technologies and promote technological self-reliance, aligning with the nation’s long-term innovation and Atmanirbhar Bharat vision.
schemeContent.benefits_md: - Loan – Debt funding (via loan or optionally convertible debt) from the SLFM, calculated as 50% of the project cost. - Equity – Funding via equity or equity linked instruments from the SLFM, calculated as 50% of the value of each funding round.

basicDetails.schemeName: Global Engagement Scheme: Festival of India

schemeContent.briefDescription: The scheme aims to provide artists practising Indian art forms with an opportunity to perform abroad. Funding for international travel, performance opportunities, and logistical support is provided to Indian artists, dancers, musicians, and cultural troupes selected for performance abroad.
schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The "Global Engagement Scheme: Festival of India" component of the Global Engagement Scheme by the ICR Division, Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to provide artists practising Indian art forms an opportunity to perform abroad under the banner of 'Festival of India'. Through this component, funding for international travel, performance opportunities, and logistical support is provided to Indian artists, dancers, musicians, and cultural troupes selected for performance abroad. The component is implemented by the Ministry of Culture in coordination with Indian Missions abroad, through a Standing Committee, a Festival of India (FOI) Cell, and a Screening Committee. > **Objectives:** - Promote Indian Culture abroad. - Strengthen bonds of foreign countries with India. - Promote bilateral cultural contracts. - Project India's cultural image abroad. - Promote inbound tourism. > **Institutional Set-up:** - A Standing Committee, chaired by the Secretary (Culture), includes representatives from ICCR, Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Planning Commission, Financial Advisor of the Ministry of Culture, DG, Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), and other related departments/agencies; it decides on the selection of countries, events, and time span. - A Festival of India Cell coordinates with participating agencies to prepare a consolidated proposal covering artist selection, delegation size, travel dates, venues, timings, logistics, accommodation, cargo handling, and other details. - A Screening Committee facilitates participation of non-government agencies/persons having expertise in performing arts, literature, and exhibitions; graded and empanelled persons are listed on the Ministry of Culture website. > **Events covered:** - Dance (classical, folk, contemporary, fusion), - Music (vocal, instrumental, sufi, classical, semi-classical, carnatic, contemporary), - Exhibitions, - Theatre, - Folk Arts including Mehendi artists and puppetry, - Literary Festival (from Sahitya Akademi), - Food Festival, - Film Festival, - Yoga, - Fashion Show/Textile Exhibition
schemeContent.benefits_md: 1. Ministry of Culture meets expenditure on the selected delegation, including international passage, performance fees, visa fee, travel insurance, cost of extra baggage, and lodging in 3 or 4 star hotels. 1. Ministry also supports venue hiring charges and publicity expenses. 1. Missions are expected to explore sponsorship through local government and/or public-private funding for venues, other infrastructure (sound system, lighting), local hospitality, and local transportation, to the extent possible, before including such expenditure in the budget — this ensures maximising the limited budget for Festival of India. 1. Indian Missions are encouraged to organize Food Festivals, Film Festival, Yoga, and Fashion Show or Textile Exhibition as part of the Festival, for which the Ministry facilitates contacts with the concerned Ministry or organization. 1. Ministry of Culture also sends cultural troupes from its Zonal Cultural Centres for folk dances/music, and from autonomous organizations such as Sangeet Natak Akademi and Kalashetra for classical dance/music; exhibitions and/or lectures through museums, Lalit Kala Akademi, or Sahitya Akademi are also supported. > **Mode of Disbursement:** - Funds are not given directly to artists; the Ministry identifies a nodal agency in India for making arrangements for international passage booking, visas, and payment of performance fees to the artists. > **Frequency/Timing of Disbursement:** - The approved budget is released in two instalments 75 percent after financial and administrative approval, and the balance on conclusion of the festival, on receipt of utilization certificates. > **Validity/Conditions:** - Ministry of Culture expects constant feedback before, during, and after the festival period; Missions should send reports, photographs, and video recordings, if made.

Objectives:
Promote Indian Culture abroad.

Institutional Set-up:

A Standing Committee, chaired by the Secretary (Culture), includes representatives from ICCR, Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Planning Commission, Financial Advisor of the Ministry of Culture, DG, Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), and other related departments/agencies; it decides on the selection of countries, events, and time span.

A Festival of India Cell coordinates with participating agencies to prepare a consolidated proposal covering artist selection, delegation size, travel dates, venues, timings, logistics, accommodation, cargo handling, and other details.

A Screening Committee facilitates participation of non-government agencies/persons having expertise in performing arts, literature, and exhibitions; graded and empanelled persons are listed on the Ministry of Culture website.
Events covered:
Dance (classical, folk, contemporary, fusion),
Music (vocal, instrumental, sufi, classical, semi-classical, carnatic, contemporary),
Exhibitions,
Theatre,
Folk Arts including Mehendi artists and puppetry,
Literary Festival (from Sahitya Akademi),
Food Festival,
Film Festival,
Yoga,
Fashion Show/Textile Exhibition

Ministry of Culture meets expenditure on the selected delegation, including international passage, performance fees, visa fee, travel insurance, cost of extra baggage, and lodging in 3 or 4 star hotels.
Ministry also supports venue hiring charges and publicity expenses.

Missions are expected to explore sponsorship through local government and/or public-private funding for venues, other infrastructure (sound system, lighting), local hospitality, and local transportation, to the extent possible, before including such expenditure in the budget — this ensures maximising the limited budget for Festival of India.

Indian Missions are encouraged to organize Food Festivals, Film Festival, Yoga, and Fashion Show or Textile Exhibition as part of the Festival, for which the Ministry facilitates contacts with the concerned Ministry or organization.

Ministry of Culture also sends cultural troupes from its Zonal Cultural Centres for folk dances/music, and from autonomous organizations such as Sangeet Natak Akademi and Kalashetra for classical dance/music; exhibitions and/or lectures through museums, Lalit Kala Akademi, or Sahitya Akademi are also supported.
Mode of Disbursement:

Funds are not given directly to artists; the Ministry identifies a nodal agency in India for making arrangements for international passage booking, visas, and payment of performance fees to the artists.
Frequency/Timing of Disbursement:
The approved budget is released in two instalments 75 percent after financial and administrative approval, and the balance on conclusion of the festival, on receipt of utilization certificates.
Validity/Conditions:

Once the dates of the Festival and suggestions from the Missions are received for activities proposed to be included, the approval of the Hon'ble Minister of Culture is obtained.

schemeContent.detailedDescription_md: The Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS) was introduced in January 2017 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, to assist the identified manual scavengers and their dependants in rehabilitation in alternative occupations. SRMS was revised in November 2013 in consonance with the provision of the “Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (MS Act, 2013).
schemeContent.benefits_md:
1. Identified manual scavengers, one from each family, are provided one-time cash assistance of ₹ 40,000.
   1. The identified manual scavengers and their dependents are provided project-based upfront capital subsidy up to ₹ 5,00,000 and concessional loans for undertaking self-employment ventures.
   1. Sanitation workers and their dependants are provided assistance for the procurement of sanitation-related projects on the same scale as admissible to manual scavengers for general tasks.
   1. The group of the target beneficiaries is eligible for projects costing up to ₹ 50,00,000.
   1. Beneficiaries are also provided training for skill development for up to two years, during which a stipend of ₹ 3,000 per month is also provided.
   1. Manual Scavengers and their family members are also eligible for Health Insurance coverage of ₹ 5,00,000 under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PMJAY)
   1. Upskilling/RPL training is provided to sanitation workers.
   1. Workshops are organized with the officers, supervisors, and sanitation workers on “Hazardous Cleaning of Sewers and Septic Tanks”.

***The rate of interest chargeable from the beneficiaries will be as follows:-***
**Range of Projects:** up to ₹1,00,000/-	
**Rate of Subsidy:** 5% per annum (4% per annum for women beneficiaries)
**Range of Projects:** above 1,00,000/-	
**Rate of Subsidy:** 6% per annum

schemeDefinitions.name: Manual Scavengers

children.text: A person engaged or employed by an individual or a local authority or an agency or a contractor, for manually cleaning, carrying, disposing of, or otherwise handling in any manner, human excreta in an insanitary latrine or in an open drain or pit into which the human excreta from the insanitary latrines is disposed of, or on railway track or in such other spaces or premises, as the Central Government or a State  Government may notify,  before the excreta fully decomposes in such a manner as may be prescribed, and the expression ‘’Manual Scavenging” shall be construed accordingly.
a)    “engaged or employed’’ means being engaged or employed on a regular or contract basis;

b)    a person engaged or employed to clean excreta with the help of such devices and using such protective gear, as the Central Government may notify on this behalf, shall not be deemed to be a ‘manual scavenger’.
